entry.title: Maurice Grau (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Metropolitan Opera director Maurice Grau (pictured) was "important in the growth of popular musical theatre in America"?

entry.title: his Connecticut TV station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that televangelist Gene Scott went 65 hours without sleep when he barricaded himself in the studios of his Connecticut TV station to protest an order to pay taxes?

entry.title: a train station in Singapore (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a train station in Singapore repeatedly had issues with the design of its stairs?

entry.title: Ho Chung Kin (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the Olympic shooter Ho Chung Kin translated more than 150 Tang-dynasty and Song-dynasty poems, maintaining a rhyme structure that mirrors the original classical Chinese texts?

entry.title: Moneka, Kansas (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that most or all of the inhabitants of Moneka, Kansas, were abolitionists?

entry.title: David of Sassoun (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that David of Sassoun has been called the most recognized symbol of Armenia, along with Mount Ararat?

entry.title: ToNiePokój escape room fire (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the deaths of five teenagers in Poland in the ToNiePokój escape room fire led to inspections of escape rooms in Lithuania and Czechia?

entry.title: Thomas M. Robins (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Thomas M. Robins was responsible for the construction of the Bonneville Dam?

entry.title: epistemology (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that according to one school of epistemology, nobody knows anything?
